subject.title: Matrix DM session-key lowercasing collides case-distinct MXIDs, sharing one peer's DM transcript with another under per-peer scope

question: Should the fix preserve case for Matrix direct MXIDs only, or also change Signal direct peer IDs in the same security-sensitive session-key boundary?
rationale: The Matrix source path and DM isolation contract are clear, but expanding the shared registry to Signal direct changes another channel's transcript/session identity semantics without equal contract proof in this review.

options.title: Fix Matrix direct first
options.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now, prove legacy folded-row safety, and leave Signal direct unchanged until a focused Signal identity proof exists.

options.title: Enroll Matrix and Signal direct
options.body: Preserve both Matrix and Signal direct IDs in one registry change, but require direct-ID contract proof and regressions for both channels before merge.

options.title: Wait for live homeserver proof
options.body: Defer code changes until a permissive Matrix homeserver demonstrates the full inbound-to-transcript-load leak, trading speed for stronger runtime evidence.

recommendation.title: Fix Matrix direct first
recommendation.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now, prove legacy folded-row safety, and leave Signal direct unchanged until a focused Signal identity proof exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent related Matrix session-key commits and PR discussion show the clearest ownership of alias safety and security-boundary decisions in this area.
